newsitem.title: CHINA: Huaxin Cement net plunges, costs up.
newsitem.headline: Huaxin Cement net plunges, costs up.

text.p: Huaxin Cement's 1996 net profit plunged 63.87 percent against 1995 based on international accounting standards due to sharp increase in costs and a weak cement market, the firm's annual report said on Tuesday.
Huaxin's 1996 net profit was 15.119 million yuan, down from 41.844 million yuan the previous year, the report published in the Shanghai Securities News said.

"Prices for coal and electricity increased by an average of 18 percent in 1996 while the selling price for cement only rose four percent, which squeezed profit margins greatly," the company statement said.

"The continued austerity measures over the past few years have reduced demand for cement, resulting in a weak market over a long period, which also had a negative impact on the company's 1996 results," it said.
Another key factor for the decline in profit was a delay in one of its production lines going into operation due to a change in design, it added.
